results.title: World Cup 2026: Brazil odds, futures, predictions, best bets for tournament - CBS Sports
highlights:
The federation has decided to give Carlo Ancelotti the reins for the 2026 World Cup campaign as Brazil try to re-establish themselves as one of the dominant forces in the game. Ancelotti has a legendary managerial record at the club level but this is his first national team gig. Brazil have gone 5-2-3 in his 10 matches at the helm. I'll look at the 2026 World Cup futures odds for Brazil, offer predictions for how far the Selecao can go and whether Ancelotti can unlock something this summer which evaded past managers.
[...]
- To win the World Cup: +900
- To reach the World Cup final: +440
- To reach the semifinal: +220
- To reach the quarterfinal: +100
- To reach the Round of 16: -260
- To win Group C: -310
[...]
Let's say Brazil go on to win Group C. They'll meet runner-up in Group F in the first knockout game, which would likely be either Japan or Tunisia. Brazil have played both sides under Ancelotti, drawing 1-1 with Tunisia and losing 3-2 to Japan in Tokyo. They would be probably still be favored against either side and if they advance, they'd play either the Group E runner-up or the Group I runner-up. Ecuador, Senegal, Norway and Ivory Coast are the most likely candidates here. Once again, Brazil would be the favorite to advance to the quarterfinal round in Miami and would likely match up against either England or Mexico.
[...]
## Best bets for Brazil at 2026 World Cup
[...]
I'm confident in Brazil winning the group, as are the oddsmakers with a -310 price. Outside of a potential draw in the opening match against Morocco, I think the Selecao will coast through Group C. If Ancelotti's tactics mesh positively with an ultra-talented squad that's healthy, getting to the quarterfinal at +100 almost feels like a lock.
[...]
I would probably hold off betting on Brazil to go farther than that until seeing how they look in the first few group games, but +220 to make the semifinal isn't a bad price prior to the World Cup kicking off. Given the potential opponents, I see Brazil facing minimal resistance until that potential quarterfinal round against either England or Mexico, teams which have historically crumbled on big stages. This Brazil team has not been at its best heading into the summer and is clouded in mystery, but the fundamentals on paper provide some reason for optimism with Ancelotti taking charge. It's probably not going to resemble the classic "jogo bonito" but if it results in a sixth World Cup title, no one will care about how the job got done.

results.title: Brazil vs Morocco Top Picks & Betting Odds – World Cup 2026 Preview - Yahoo Sports
highlights:
By Matchday 3 in Group C, both Brazil and Morocco will likely know exactly what they need. Brazil enter as the group’s most decorated side and the team the market expects to advance, but a slow start or an early stumble could mean this fixture carries knockout-round weight before the knockout round arrives. Morocco, fresh off their historic 2022 semi-final run and now arriving as African champions, will be targeting nothing less than a second successive deep tournament run, and a result here would send a statement to every contender left in the draw.
[...]
Brazil vs Morocco odds make the Selecao clear favorites at -145, and the underlying evidence supports that price: Carlo Ancelotti’s side carry vastly superior World Cup pedigree and an attacking roster that Morocco’s remodelled defence will struggle to contain across 90 minutes. Brazil to win is the headline pick, with the case for under 2.5 goals equally compelling given Morocco’s defensive identity and the tournament-stage caution both sides will exercise.
[...]
The game is likely to be won or lost in the space between Morocco’s defensive block and Brazil’s creative midfield. If Ancelotti’s side can draw Morocco out with patient ball circulation and then exploit the width through Vinicius Junior and Raphinha, the goals will come. Morocco’s best route to a result is to stay compact, transition quickly through Achraf Hakimi’s overlapping runs, and hope Brahim Diaz can conjure something from limited possession.

results.title: Spain vs Cabo Verde 2026 Preview, Odds & Prediction
highlights:
One of the most striking first-round matchups at the 2026 FIFA World Cup pits Spain vs Cabo Verde — reigning European champions and tournament favorites — against Cabo Verde, who are making their historic debut on football’s grandest stage. This Group H clash on June 15 promises a clash between world-class technical football and the fearless ambition of a nation playing in its first-ever World Cup.
[...]
| Attribute | Spain | Cabo Verde |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FIFA Ranking | #1 | ~#68 |
| World Cup Experience | 16 tournaments (1 title — 2010) | 1st appearance (2026) |
| Coach | Luis de la Fuente | Bubista |
| UEFA/CAF Tournament | Euro 2024 Champions | AFCON QF (x2) |
| World Cup Odds to Win | +450 (favorites) | ~2000/1 |
| Key Strength | Possession, pressing, depth | Defensive organization, counter-attack |
| Squad depth | Top-tier European talent | Mix of European/MLS diaspora |
[...]
Spain are overwhelming favorites to win this Group H opener, and the underlying data supports that assessment. La Roja’s squad depth is unmatched at this tournament — their forward line alone (Yamal, Williams, Olmo, Oyarzabal) could trouble any defense in the world, and Rodri’s return to fitness gives them a control mechanism that makes even high-pressure opponents look disorganized.
[...]
That said, Cabo Verde will not simply capitulate. Their emotional motivation at their first-ever World Cup will be immense, and if they can stay organized in the opening 20–25 minutes and keep the score level heading into the final third, they may find Spain growing impatient and vulnerable to a transition. The 4–2 loss to Chile in March showed a defensive fragility when faced with high-press, direct football — exactly what Spain will deploy.
[...]
Predicted outcome: Spain 3–0 Cabo Verde. Lamine Yamal is expected to be decisive, with Spain’s midfield dominance stifling Cabo Verde’s counter-attacking threat. The Blue Sharks will compete hard but the gap in quality is simply too wide for a debut nation against reigning European champions.
[...]
Spain enter as massive favorites for this match, with FanDuel Sportsbook listing Spain at -6000 in the Tie No Bet market and the “Cape Verde and Draw” double chance at +750. Spain’s tournament odds to lift the World Cup sit at +450, making them the outright global favorites.
[...]
A: Spain are listed as the outright favorites at +450 (FanDuel Sportsbook) to win the 2026 World Cup, an implied probability of 18.18%.
